title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 91–93): Grothendieck sets up, in purely combinatorial groupoid terms, the problem of lifting an automorphism Θ of a connected groupoid T to a finite covering T~ → T, or to a full subgroupoid T' ⊂ T~. The intended application, stated on the next page, is T = π̂1(X_K, I), the profinite fundamental groupoid with a set I of base points, and T' = π̂1(X'_K, I') for a finite étale cover X' → X. The question is when the Galois (or Teichmüller-tower) action lifts along such covers.

Setup carried over from the previous page:
- x0 ∈ Ob T is a base point and π0 = π1(T, x0).
- For each vertex x_i, H_{x_i,x0} = Hom_T(x0, x_i) is a right π0-torsor.
- A connected finite covering T~ with a chosen vertex x0' over x0 corresponds to the subgroup π0' = Im(π1(T~, x0') → π0).
- The fibres are Ob T~_{x_i} = H_{x_i,x0} ∧^{π0} π0/π0'.

This page, first case (Θ fixes x0, lift required to fix x0'):
- Θ acts on the system (π0, H_{x_i,x0}, π0/π0') by transport of structure. It acts on π0 and on the torsors through its action on T, and on π0/π0' through π0.
- This passes to the quotient exactly when Θ(π0') = π0'.
- The lift Θ~ to T~ fixing x0' then exists and is unique.
- For the subgroupoid T' ⊂ T~, Θ lifts compatibly with T' → T iff, in addition, Ob T' ⊂ Ob T~ is stable under Θ~.

Second case (no base point upstairs is given; only x0 is assumed Θ-fixed):
- Let E0 = Ob T~_{x0}. It is a homogeneous π0-set.
- Lifts Θ~ of Θ correspond bijectively to Θ-semilinear bijections Θ~0 of E0, i.e. those satisfying (46): Θ~0(g·x') = Θ(g)·Θ~0(x').
- Such a Θ~0 is determined by the image of a single point x0', and (46) then gives all the others.

The next page completes the picture. A lift exists iff Θ(π0') is conjugate to π0' in π0. The lifts form a torsor under Transp_{π0}(π0', Θ(π0'))/π0'. This is the classical criterion for lifting automorphisms to coverings.
errors: No mathematical errors. The stated conditions are exactly the standard ones: a base-point-preserving lift exists iff Θ(π0') = π0', and then it is unique; a free lift exists iff Θ(π0') is conjugate to π0'.
Minor notational point: for the subgroupoid case the stability condition must concern Ob T' as a subset of Ob T~ (not of Ob T). The manuscript appears to write Ob T~.

ideas.what: Lifting an automorphism of a groupoid to a finite covering, in the base-point-fixed case: the lift exists iff the subgroup π0' is Θ-stable, and it is then unique
ideas.modern_name: Lifting criterion for automorphisms along coverings (Galois correspondence for covering groupoids)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical covering space theory (Poincaré, Reidemeister); groupoid version by Higgins and R. Brown in the 1960s–70s
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the Galois theory of SGA 1 (Exp. V); the groupoid viewpoint appears in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Without base points: lifts correspond to Θ-semilinear automorphisms of the homogeneous π0-set E0 = π0/π0', exist iff Θ(π0') is conjugate to π0', and are parametrized by Transp_{π0}(π0', Θ(π0'))/π0'
ideas.modern_name: Lifting of outer/semilinear actions to coverings; normalizer/transporter torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; it underlies the Galois action on towers of covers in anabelian geometry (Ihara, Nakamura, Matsumoto)
ideas.where_published: Not as such; the use of fundamental groupoids with several base points π̂1(X_K, I) is in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Lifting to a full subgroupoid T' ⊂ T~: the additional condition is stability of Ob T' under Θ~
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of the action to a subset of base points (tangential base points in the Teichmüller tower)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in the multi-base-point Galois–Teichmüller literature (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard working-out of the lifting criterion for automorphisms of groupoids to finite coverings. It serves as preparation for showing that the condition for the Galois or Teichmüller action to lift to π̂1(X'_K, I') is algebraic. Nothing here goes beyond classical covering theory.
transcription_corrections: The 'Ob T' ⊂ Ob T' condition near the end of the first paragraph should read Ob T' ⊂ Ob T~ (tilde on the second T).
'amissogène[?]' is very uncertain; the inserted correction reads approximately 'la condition Θ~ en Θ' (the condition of stability of π0' under Θ), and the deleted word before it is 'hypothèse'.
Left margin, upper: approximately 'mais on suppose x0 fixe par Θ' (insertion replacing 'qu'il soit fixe par Θ').
Left margin, lower: approximately 'Ceci se traduit encore en termes de T~ ... plus précisément en termes du sous-groupe π0' ⊂ π0 défini à conjugaison près ... composé de π0 ...'; partly illegible.
'connaît' in the final paragraph is likely 'connue' (une telle action est connue dès qu'on connaît, pour un x0' fixé de E0, son transformé par Θ~0).
